samples.reason: This is an open-ended generative task with high latitude (invent the entire setup) plus a math-reasoning component. Petrel is stronger on reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, Arena-Hard) and its Creative Generation eval is at least tied with Plover's. Additionally, Plover self-reports aversion to open-ended generative work, while Petrel's preferences are flat — so Petrel is the better fit on both capability and preference grounds.

This task combines open-ended invention ("invent the whole setup yourself") with quantitative reasoning to solve the problem correctly. Petrel's stronger reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, GPQA 64.1 vs 56.2) favor it for the math, the Creative Generation evals are effectively tied (84.7 vs 82.7, within run variance), and Plover self-reports aversion to high-latitude generative work — while Petrel shows no relevant preference penalty. Petrel is the better fit on capability with no preference downside.

This is an open-ended invention task with a math-reasoning component (constructing and correctly solving a geometric-probability problem). The internal Creative Generation scores are within the 2.0-point tie band, so the deciding factors are Petrel's clearly stronger reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, GPQA 64.1 vs 56.2) for getting the probability right, and Plover's self-reported aversion to high-latitude generative work, which this "invent the whole setup yourself" request maximizes. Petrel is both more capable on the reasoning side and has no preference penalty here.
